events.title: The Elegance of Erickson Exhibition
events.address: 124 West Main Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
The Elegance of Erickson Exhibition is a celebration of handmade art glass by Carl Erickson and his team of glass masters at the Erickson Glass Works (1943-1961) in Bremen, Ohio. Erickson Glass Works was a renowned mid-century American studio art glass company. In 1906, at the age of 7, master glassblower Carl Erickson immigrated with his family from Reimyre, Sweden. He grew up in a family of master glassblowers, and at the age of 14, began his American career working as an apprentice alongside his father at the Pairpoint Manufacturing Company in New Bedford, Massachusetts.

 

The Ohio Glass Museum and Glass Blowing Studio is pleased to present this exhibition in honor of the Erickson Glass Works. The exhibition is made possible by the generous gifts of glass permanently donated to their archives by the following collectors: Elizabeth Norman, Paula and Rick Barnhart, Jeff Ulrich, Dave Shannon in memory of Faye Hillyard-Shannon. Visitors can view dynamic exhibits, watch daily live glassblowing demonstrations, shop for local handmade glass art, and participate in interactive studio classes in both glassblowing and fused glass. events.title: Color Improvisations 3: A Major Exhibition of Contemporary Quilts
events.address: 145 East Main Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
Color Improvisations 3: A Major Exhibition of Contemporary Quilts features 38 large quilts that explore color, scale, and improvisation in contemporary textile art. Curated by internationally recognized artist Nancy Crow, the exhibition at the Decorative Arts Center of Ohio includes works by quiltmakers from the United States, Canada, and New Zealand, highlighting the creativity, innovation and artistic excellence shaping contemporary quilt making today. Using bold abstract forms and richly worked fabrics, the artists balance exquisite skill with creative risk. Their quilts invite viewers to experience color as movement, texture, and feeling. This exhibition will run from October 3rd, 2026 to January 3rd, 2027.

 

For more information, please visit the Decorative Arts Center of Ohio’s website.

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.title: James McNeill Whistler (Exhibition on Screen)
events.desc:
In an era of great change and great beauty emerged the character of James McNeill Whistler. Considered by some to be one of the great innovators of 19th century art, he was a contemporary of the Impressionists, much admired by Van Gogh and Manet. Boldly experimental and famously witty, Whistler disrupted the strict conventions of Victorian society in pursuit of a new cult of beauty, creating “art for art’s sake” and earning himself a place in the history of great art. He found a parallel between painting and music, and entitled many of his paintings “arrangements”, “harmonies” and “nocturnes”, emphasizing the importance of tonal harmony in his work. 
 
Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. 
 
Made in close collaboration with Tate Britain, directed by David Bickerstaff https://worthington.org/calendar.aspx?EID=9450

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.desc:
In our lives, we are both always experts and novices. Personal essay and book-length memoirs allow writers to explore compelling, central moments, experiences, and material from their lives to communicate meaning, universal themes, and takeaways to readers, transforming experience into narrative art. What are the ethics of writing about others? We will explore conventions of the form, such as self-disclosure and deep examination, creating tension, character arc, using scenes and dialogue, distilling the “one big thing” your piece is about, and the blurry boundaries of fact and imagination in creative nonfiction—the only writing form defined by what it is not. Discussion questions may include: how do you maximize self-inquiry while avoiding “navel gazing”? What elements make stories engaging to readers? How do you craft a persona on the page?

By the end of the session, you will possess an understanding of personal essay and memoir writing fundamentals: honesty, self-reflection, tension, balancing scenes and exposition, distilling your memoir or essay’s “about-ness” (i.e., theme), and what to include versus what to omit. Ironically, as the Allies’ vise grip closes on Bertie and his family, their only salvation is to flee to the United States. events.desc:
This month, Roundtable regular Ed Showman will give a talk on the Battle of Shiloh. Shiloh was the bloodiest battle in American history up to that point. After a surprise Confederate attack, Sherman rallied his troops on the first day and helped lead the Union counterattack the next morning. His performance at Shiloh helped restore his reputation after his troubled command in Kentucky. Grant, meanwhile, faced criticism over the army’s lack of preparedness and the heavy casualties. Everyone is welcome to attend and admission is $5 at the door. This event will be held at the Sherman House Museum. 

To learn more, please visit the Fairfield County Heritage Association’s Facebook page.

events.title: Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: The Crucible
events.desc:

Set during the Salem witch trials of 1692, The Crucible is Arthur Miller’s gripping drama about fear, power, and the consequences of mass hysteria. As accusations of witchcraft spread through a small Puritan town, neighbors turn against one another, reputations are destroyed, and impossible choices must be made in the pursuit of truth and justice. A timeless American classic, The Crucible explores the dangers of suspicion, the cost of integrity, and the courage it takes to stand by one’s convictions. events.venue: Davidson Theater –  Riffe Center Theatre Complex
events.desc:

This world premiere and unique collaboration between CAPA, BalletMet and European production company ODD Continent reimagines Grammy-winner Sheryl Crow’s most powerful songs – from “Steve McQueen” to “Strong Enough” – through drama, ballet, and live on-stage music.

Ordinary Woman is the story of estranged midwestern sisters who must reconcile conflicting memories of the past when forced back together by environmental and social unrest.

The exhibition features more than 60 portraits of post-9/11 service members and Veterans, each one hand painted by President Bush and paired with a personal story of service, sacrifice, and resilience written by the former president.

The NVMM is open Thursday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

events.address: 506 North High Street, Lancaster, OH, USA
events.desc:
Mystical Infusions: A Tisane and Tea Blending Workshop

Boundless Moon and The Boundless Shoppe invite you to Mystical Infusions, an enchanting workshop where the art of tea and tisane blending comes to life. This unique experience, led by certified herbalist Christina Powell, offers the perfect way to embrace the holiday season. Dive into the world of teas and tisanes, uncover their secrets, and craft your own personalized blends. At the end of the workshop, you’ll take home two beautifully crafted 4-ounce jars of your unique tea blends.

Tickets are priced at $50 per person. You can make your reservations here. Please note a 24-hour cancellation policy is in place due to the time, energy, and resources required to execute these events. Whether you’re a tea aficionado or a novice eager to learn, Mystical Infusions offers a magical journey into the world of teas and tisanes.

events.title: Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: The Crucible
events.desc:
Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: The Crucible on November 19th-22nd at the Lancaster City Parks office! Set during the Salem witch trials of 1692, The Crucible is Arthur Miller’s gripping drama about fear, power, and the consequences of mass hysteria. As accusations of witchcraft spread through a small Puritan town, neighbors turn against one another, reputations are destroyed, and impossible choices must be made in the pursuit of truth and justice. A timeless American classic, The Crucible explores the dangers of suspicion, the cost of integrity, and the courage it takes to stand by one’s convictions. Powerful, thought-provoking, and deeply relevant, this unforgettable play continues to resonate with audiences today. Tickets will sell quickly, so be sure to reserve your seat today! This show is recommended for teens and adults due to mature themes and intense dramatic content.

For more information, please visit Rise Up Arts Alliance’s Facebook page.

events.title: Ordinary Woman
events.venue: Davidson Theater –  Riffe Center Theatre Complex
events.desc:
An extraordinary new musical featuring the songs of Sheryl Crow.

This world premiere and unique collaboration between CAPA, BalletMet and European production company ODD Continent reimagines Grammy-winner Sheryl Crow’s most powerful songs – from “Steve McQueen” to “Strong Enough” – through drama, ballet, and live on-stage music.

Ordinary Woman is the story of estranged midwestern sisters who must reconcile conflicting memories of the past when forced back together by environmental and social unrest.

Made in Columbus by a local and international team, including BalletMet artistic director Remi Wörtmeyer, Ordinary Woman plays a very limited run of three performances only. Don’t miss your chance to see it before the rest of the world!

Whether you’ve joined them before or you’re stepping into meditation for the first time, you’re invited to come as you are and make space to slow down, breathe, and reconnect. Each Monday, they’ll gather in the Gathering Place for an hour of meditation, mindfulness, meaningful conversation, and practical tools you can carry with you long after the evening ends. No experience is needed. There’s no pressure to have meditation “figured out.” Just find a comfortable spot, settle in, and give yourself the gift of being present.

events.title: Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
events.desc:
The Teen Advisory Board (TAB) is a group of teenage volunteers who collaborate with library staff on programs, services, and resources relevant to teens. The primary goal of a Teen Advisory Board is to give teens a voice in shaping the library's offerings, ensuring the library remains engaging and responsive to the needs of its younger customers. Members share ideas, help plan teen events, suggest new books or media, and make a difference in the community, all while developing leadership and teamwork skills. 

TAB is open to all teens in grades 7-12. Through this process, teens will sign up as volunteers and earn volunteer hours if needed. Teens may join TAB at any time throughout the year.

Meetings will occur on the last Tuesday of each month at both locations from 5:00-6:00 p.m. Teens should choose one location, either Pickerington Main Library or Sycamore Plaza Library, as their home base for TAB and attend all meetings there.

events.title: Vanillekipferl Cookie Making at Keller Market House
events.address: 134 South Columbus Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
Learn to create traditional Vanillekipferl from Austria with Danielle of the European Cottage Bakery at this workshop in Keller Market House! Vanillekipferl is a beloved traditional Christmas cookie made with nuts that has gained popularity in other countries. In this class, you’ll learn how to shape and roll the cookie dough into ropes and cut them individually to roll them out by hand for shaping, how to bake them, and how to cover them in sugar without breaking them and without sprinkling powder sugar on top. You will get your cookies all prepared here in the workshop, and then take them home to bake. You will need powdered sugar at home to finish.

You will also receive recipes to make marzipan from scratch and ideas for how to use it, plus a recipe to make Rumtopf (which takes a minimum of 3 months to create before using it) or dumplings. Tickets are $40 to the general public and $35 for friend of the market members. Register online today before seats sell out! The registration deadline is Saturday, November 28th. events.title: NOVEL CONVERSATION
events.desc:
The Stolen Life of Colette Marceau
by
Kristin Harmel

Colette Marceau has been stealing jewels for nearly as long as she can remember, following the centuries-old code of honor instilled in her by her mother, take only from the cruel and unkind, and give to those in need. Never was their family tradition more important than seven decades earlier, during the Second World War, when Annabel and Colette worked side by side in Paris to fund the French Resistance.

But one night in 1942, it all went wrong. Annabel was arrested by the Germans, and Colette’s four-year-old sister, Liliane, disappeared in the chaos of the raid, along with an exquisite diamond bracelet sewn into the hem of her nightgown for safekeeping. Soon after, Annabel was executed, and Liliane’s body was found floating in the Seine—but the bracelet was nowhere to be found.

Seventy years later, Colette—who has “redistributed” $30 million in jewels over the decades to fund many worthy organizations—has done her best to put her tragic past behind her, but her life begins to unravel when the long-missing bracelet suddenly turns up in a museum exhibit in Boston. If Colette can discover where it has been all this time—and who

events.desc:
The Homework Help Center is a community resource that serves the entire Pickerington Local School District. Unlike tutoring services that provide one-on-one help in specific subject areas, the Library’s Homework Help service supports students by ensuring they are able to complete specific work assigned by their classroom teachers. 

Library staff and volunteers are knowledgeable in guiding students through homework assignments in many subjects and grade levels. If the subject material is beyond the knowledge of staff and volunteers or students need more individual assistance than we can provide, we can direct them to resources for additional help.

events.title: ROX: Ruling Our eXperiences
events.desc:
R.O.X. “Ruling Our eXperiences” is a non-profit, educational program for girls. During the 20-week curriculum, participants will be equipped with knowledge on topics such as confidence, healthy communications, navigating relationships, goal setting, and self-defense. Open to girls in grades 7-12.

Facilitated by Sycamore Plaza Library’s Teen Services Librarian, participants will meet on Thursdays from 6:00-7:00 p.m. to engage in guided discussions and activities based on the R.O.X. curriculum. 

The program is free and open to girls in grades 7-12. If you or your teen is interested, please contact Amanda at Sycamore Plaza Library in person or via email at amcevoy@pickeringtonlibrary.org.

Registering for this event does not guarantee your spot. Amanda will reach out to you with additional paperwork and information.

To learn more about R.O.X. please visit their website: Ruling Our eXperiences (ROX). 

Thank you to South Central Power for graciously providing a grant for registration costs.

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: Watercolor Holiday Cards
events.desc:
Create four holiday-themed greeting cards using watercolor pencils in this guided class with artist Deb Waites. Discover the artist within you in this fun and interactive watercolor pencil class. Guided by experienced artist Deb Waites, participants will create four Holiday cards perfect for giving to friends and loved ones or displaying in a frame at home. To help you get started, everyone will begin with a pre-sketched picture, making it easy to focus on coloring, shading, and blending.

Through hands-on creativity, you’ll experiment with color and the unique effects watercolor pencils can create when combined with water. Perfect for beginners and experienced artists alike, this class is a great opportunity to try something new and enjoy the creative process. All materials will be provided—just bring your curiosity and creativity!

Adults only. Class size is limited. Registration is required.

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!
events.desc:
A family friendly event! Step into the holiday hilarity of Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!, Good Medicine Productions’ wildly interactive twist on Charles Dickens’ beloved classic. This isn’t a show where you sit quietly in the dark—it’s a Christmas party where the audience becomes part of the story.

events.title: A Rock Mill Holiday
events.desc:
Take a break from the hustle and bustle of the holiday season with a visit to this historical site – Stebelton Park at Rock Mill – a restored gristmill from the early 1800s. Cookies and hot drinks will be served. The park is open year-round during daylight hours. The mill, though, is only open during “Rock Mill Days” or special events such as this one. The 2026 season has ended but will resume in 2027.

Rock Mill stands at least 90’ above the gorge of Hocking River Falls. In 1905, it closed for business and fell into disrepair. After a decade-long restoration effort ending in 2017, it roared to life and milled grain again for the first time in over 100 years! Come see this amazing piece of history, enjoy the view from Rock Mill Covered Bridge and the beautiful setting! Bring your own drinking water. Potable water is not available at this location. There is no heat inside the mill so be sure to dress for the weather, including footwear. Pets are welcome in the park but are not allowed inside Rock Mill. Pets must be under control at all times and on a leash no longer than 6’. For the health and safety of all, pick up and properly dispose of pets’ waste.

events.title: Blood on the Clocktower
events.desc:
On a stormy night, a shriek echoes through the town. Everyone rushes to the clock tower to find their beloved storyteller has been murdered, lying still at its base. The villagers realize some evil has been unleashed on their town. By day, this evil looks like one of their own, but by night, it goes about, picking them off one by one. Can they identify the killer? Or will evil overrun this town in the end?

Blood on the Clocktower is an award-winning social deduction game in which a group of people works together to try to discover which one of them is the demon in their midst. During the game, you are either a "good" townsperson with roles that help you discover and share information with other "good" townspeople, or you are "evil" and try to sow lies and distrust among the other players. Each side wins when the other team is eliminated.

Each session usually runs 60 to 90 minutes. You can expect to:

Discover what Blood on the Clocktower is.

Learn how to play this game.

Meet new people through the cooperative gameplay.

Enjoy an afternoon of murder and mystery.

Great for the whole family, this early literacy class will get children ages 2 - 5 excited about reading! We feature talking, singing, reading, writing, and playing to help your child assemble the necessary building blocks of early literacy. Open to children, their caregivers, and siblings. events.title: Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief’s Tribute to America’s Warriors

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: Crafternoon & Cinema

events.address: 3550 Blacklick-Eastern Rd NE, Millersport, OH 43046, USA

Step into a Christmas story unlike any other at The Pines at Buckeye Ridge! Your journey begins inside their beautifully decorated Christmas Story Barn, where you’ll travel through three magical chapters filled with beloved Christmas characters, including Rudolph, the Misfit Toys, the Abominable Snow Monster, the magical world of Whoville and the Grinch, and their old friend Mr. Tree. events.title: The Vision Board Social at The Molt and Moon
events.desc:
Take a break from the holiday hustle and join The Molt and Moon for an evening of wine, light bites, meaningful conversation, and vision boarding! Whether you’re feeling inspired by what’s ahead, looking for a fresh perspective, or simply excited to meet new people, this is an opportunity to connect with yourself and others in a welcoming, relaxed atmosphere. The evening will be guided by Kaley, a certified Life Coach passionate about self-discovery, personal growth, and meaningful connection. Gather inspiration and explore possibilities for the year ahead, taking home a visual representation of what you’d like more of in your life. No coaching experience or artistic skills needed! Tickets are $25 per person and includes wine, light bites, all vision board supplies, and a 22×28 poster – yours to take home! Space will be limited to 15 spots to create an intimate and welcoming experience. Reserve your spot today and join them for an evening of connection, creativity, and possibility. For more information, please visit The Molt and Moon’s Facebook page.

events.title: Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!
events.desc:
A family friendly event! Step into the holiday hilarity of Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!, Good Medicine Productions’ wildly interactive twist on Charles Dickens’ beloved classic. This isn’t a show where you sit quietly in the dark—it’s a Christmas party where the audience becomes part of the story.

Filled with quick wit, outrageous characters, live music, and joyful audience participation, Uptown Scrooge delivers all the heart of Dickens with a healthy dose of laughter. Whether you’re cheering on Tiny Tim, booing Nephew Fred or finding yourself unexpectedly pulled into the action, every performance is a one-of-a-kind experience.

Perfect for families, homeschool groups, date nights, office parties, and anyone looking to laugh their way into the Christmas spirit, Uptown Scrooge:Abridged! reminds us that it’s never too late to choose generosity, joy & silliness.

events.desc:

Enjoy the evening as L-City Coffee+ serves up free hot chocolate from their wagon. Kids can stop by the Fairfield County District Library for holiday crafts and a special reading of the Christmas Story from Santa himself. This portion of the event is open to anyone.

 

At check-in at First United Methodist Church at 5:45 p.m., stroll participants will receive a bracelet granting access to a series of inspiring performances inside Lancaster’s historic churches—each one beautifully adorned for the season. The opening program begins First United Methodist Church, followed by visits to St. John’s Episcopal, First Presbyterian, and St. Peter’s Lutheran, before a grand finale at St. Mary’s Catholic Church. Along the way, guides will lead each color-coded group through the softly lit streets of Historic Square 13, where visitors can also enjoy the Advent Window Walk,

events.desc:
Take a musical trip this holiday season as the Lancaster Men’s Chorus presents “Christmas Around the World,”  its annual Christmas concert at 3 p.m. on Sunday, December 13th at Fairfield Christian Church. With holiday songs ranging from traditional to whimsical, the LMC,  under the direction of Mark Severance, will present an afternoon of family entertainment for all ages. This year’s concert will also feature the Bloom-Carroll High School Chamber Singers, under the direction of Mark Yoder.

 

The concert will include music from Spain, Austria, Germany, England and the Caribbean, in addition to songs that have originated in the United States. The LMC Christmas concert provides an opportunity for the whole family to share an experience and create memories that can be enjoyed for years and raise scholarship money for local students. Some of the songs of the Christmas concert include the annual favorite, Raindeer of the Roof, and Where Are You Christmas, God Rest You Merry Gentlemen, Hark the Herald Angels Sing, Chillin’ Like a Snowman, Carol of the Bells, Adeste Fideles, Various Themes on Fa LaLa, and, of course, Silent Night.

 

This is the 60th year for the Lancaster Men’s Chorus

events.desc:
Join Keller Market House for a festive, hands-on workshop where you’ll learn how to craft one-of-a-kind herbal gifts for your loved ones! Students will craft a gorgeous holiday bath soak layered in jars with botanicals, skin-loving clays, and magnesium salts, plus a fragrant simmer pot sachet filled with wintry herbs and spices to cozy the home with natural scent and seasonal cheer. events.title: November Project Scioto Mile Free Workout
events.desc:
November Project is a free outside fitness group that started in Boston in 2011 to break down barriers to movement! Now in 53 cities around the globe, we create free, fun, scalable (adjustable to your fitness level) workouts for all ages – and doggos!

Our workout starts at 6:14a every Wednesday morning in Genoa Park on the Scioto Mile (on the steps behind COSI). We work out for 45 minutes together until 7am, then walk down to One Line Coffee to hang out before work!

Come join us if you’re an off-the-couch fitness newbie, a runner looking to cross-train, or any fitness level in between, we’d love to see you!

events.title: Reading for Change
events.desc:
The Reading for Change Book Discussion Group explores race, ethnicity, equity, and inclusion through thoughtful discussion. Participants will deepen their understanding of systemic racism and social justice, reflect on their roles in these systems, and identify ways to create meaningful change. The group meets monthly, spending two to three months on each book to allow for deeper conversation and community impact. Meetings are held on the last Wednesday of the month at 1:00.

In November and December we will be discussing The Lilac People by Milo Todd. 

In the final days of World War II, with their freedom in sight, Bertie and Sofie find a young trans man collapsed on their property, still dressed in Holocaust prison clothes. They vow to protect him, not from the Nazis,
but from the Allied forces who are arresting queer prisoners while liberating the rest of the country. Ironically, as the Allies’ vise grip closes on Bertie and his family, their only salvation is to flee to the United States. events.title: Laughter Wellness
events.desc:
Join certified Laughter Yoga teacher, breathologist, and internationally recognized storyteller Lyn Ford for a joyful, restorative, and relaxing 60-minute session designed to support your physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being, your creativity, and your connection with others.

This accessible, chair-based workshop includes deep breathing, gentle stretching, rhythmic clapping, and playful laughter exercises that are safe and adaptable for all fitness and mobility levels. Writing prompts will also be incorporated into the session to encourage reflection and creative expression.

Together, we’ll explore easy, replicable techniques to relieve stress and anxiety, lift our spirits, increase our imaginative thinking, and build community—because laughter truly is a universal language. Laughter Wellness is perfect for anyone seeking fun and joyful self-care.

No mats or equipment are needed—just wear comfortable clothing and come ready to play!

Laughter Wellness is open to adults and teens ages 14+.

The NVMM is open Thursday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

In Reading Buddies, children in kindergarten through 4th grade build confidence and improve their reading skills by reading one-on-one with a volunteer or staff member. Kids can bring a favorite book from home or pick one off the library shelves, then enjoy a 20-minute session of reading practice. It’s a great way to develop skills, share stories, and make reading fun. 

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: ROX: Ruling Our eXperiences
events.desc:
R.O.X. “Ruling Our eXperiences” is a non-profit, educational program for girls. During the 20-week curriculum, participants will be equipped with knowledge on topics such as confidence, healthy communications, navigating relationships, goal setting, and self-defense. Open to girls in grades 7-12.

Facilitated by Sycamore Plaza Library’s Teen Services Librarian, participants will meet on Thursdays from 6:00-7:00 p.m. to engage in guided discussions and activities based on the R.O.X. curriculum. 

The program is free and open to girls in grades 7-12. If you or your teen is interested, please contact Amanda at Sycamore Plaza Library in person or via email at amcevoy@pickeringtonlibrary.org.

Registering for this event does not guarantee your spot. Amanda will reach out to you with additional paperwork and information.

To learn more about R.O.X. please visit their website: Ruling Our eXperiences (ROX). 

Thank you to South Central Power for graciously providing a grant for registration costs.

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: DIY Spa Gifts
events.desc:
Plants and natural ingredients have been used for generations to care for the body. Discover how they can become thoughtful handmade gifts. In this hands-on workshop, explore the traditional uses and benefits of botanical oils and essential oils while creating your own personalized bath and body products. 

Participants will make two body scrubs using their choice of salt, sugar, or coffee bases, along with botanical and essential oils. You’ll also create two shower steamers and receive reusable silicone molds to continue crafting at home.

Make one set to enjoy yourself and one to share with someone special, connecting with the tradition of giving handmade gifts. Each participant will take home two personalized body scrubs, two shower steamers, and reusable molds.

Sheena Hanscel is an Indigenous educator, herbalist, and founder of The Pollen Patch, an urban educational space and native ethnobotanical garden in Columbus, Ohio. Through hands-on workshops and storytelling, Sheena makes plant knowledge approachable and practical, sharing skills for creating teas, preparing simple remedies, and recognizing the plants growing all around us. Join her to explore the healing relationships

events.title: Smartphone and Tablet Essentials
events.desc:

events.title: Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!
events.desc:
A family friendly event! Step into the holiday hilarity of Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!, Good Medicine Productions’ wildly interactive twist on Charles Dickens’ beloved classic. This isn’t a show where you sit quietly in the dark—it’s a Christmas party where the audience becomes part of the story.

Filled with quick wit, outrageous characters, live music, and joyful audience participation, Uptown Scrooge delivers all the heart of Dickens with a healthy dose of laughter. Whether you’re cheering on Tiny Tim, booing Nephew Fred or finding yourself unexpectedly pulled into the action, every performance is a one-of-a-kind experience.

Perfect for families, homeschool groups, date nights, office parties, and anyone looking to laugh their way into the Christmas spirit, Uptown Scrooge:Abridged! reminds us that it’s never too late to choose generosity, joy & silliness.

events.title: Jingle All The Way Tour with Cork & Tap Excursions
events.address: 1581 Parkland Drive, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States
events.desc:
It’s that time of the year to get your tickets for Cork & Tap Excursion’s Jingle All The Way Winery tours! On Sunday, December 20th, they will visit Rockside Winery and Vineyards, Rhonemus Cellars and Buckeye Lake Winery. Last year this event sold out very quickly, so don’t wait too long to reserve your spot! Purchase your tickets today!

 

For more information, please visit Cork & Tap Excursion’s Facebook page.

events.title: Paint and Sip at Buckeye Lake Winery
events.address: 13750 Rosewood Dr NE, Thornville, Ohio 43076, United States
events.desc:
Join for a relaxing and creative afternoon at Buckeye Lake Winery for their Paint & Sip event on Sunday, December 20th! This event is open to the public and perfect for a fun outing with friends or a unique way to unwind. Tickets are $40 per person and includes 2 hours of guided instruction and one glass of wine with purchase. Purchase your ticket today before they sell out! No experience necessary—just bring your creativity and they’ll provide everything else you need. Come sip, paint, and enjoy the beautiful setting at Buckeye Lake Winery!

 

For more information, please visit Buckeye Lake Winery’s Facebook page.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club at Juniper & Ivy Coffeehouse
events.address: 200 North Main Street, Baltimore, Ohio 43105, United States
events.desc:
Meet at Juniper & Ivy Coffeehouse once a month to dive in to the vivid and enchanting worlds of Sci-Fi and Fantasy (Romantacy is made up…it’s all fantasy) and discuss your favorites. October will be Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir and November will be A House in the Cerulean Sea by TJ Klune.

 

For more information, please visit Juniper & Ivy’s Facebook page.

events.title: Lancaster Community Band Holiday Concert
events.address: Faith Memorial Church, West Fair Avenue, Lancaster, OH, USA
events.desc: Enjoy free, live music during the Lancaster Community Band’s Holiday Concert on Sunday, December 20th! The concert will start at 2 p.m. at the Faith Memorial Church on West Fair Avenue. This program is directed by Judy Rehrer and the Assistant Director is Craig McKenzie.

events.title: Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: A Christmas Carol
events.desc:
Experience the timeless story of A Christmas Carol, a heartwarming tale of redemption, generosity, and the true spirit of the holiday season, presented by Rise Up Arts Alliance at the Lancaster City Parks office! Follow the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge as a visit from three mysterious spirits leads him on an unforgettable journey through his past, present, and future—revealing that it’s never too late to change. Filled with memorable characters, festive cheer, and a message that has inspired generations, this beloved holiday classic is perfect for audiences of all ages. Tickets will sell quickly, so be sure to reserve your spot today! Join Rise Up Arts Alliance as they bring this cherished Christmas tradition to life on stage and celebrate the joy, hope, and wonder of the season.

For more information, please visit Rise Up Arts Alliance’s Facebook page.

All skill levels welcome even though meetings are communal, not instructional.

events.title: What Is Modern AI?
events.desc:
This four-part series hosted by the Library's Technology Trainer breaks down the basics of artificial intelligence through hands-on demos. Whether you're curious, skeptical, or ready to take your knowledge to the next level, you'll learn to navigate AI tools with confidence and ease.

Part 1: What is artificial intelligence (AI)? What is machine learning? What's the difference between the two?
Part 2: What are the laws, ethical concerns, and obligations surrounding AI?
Part 3: What popular AI tools are available to you, and how can you use them? We'll discuss Claude, ChatGPT, Midjourney, Gemini, and CoPilot.
Part 4: How can you create prompts for ChatGPT, Claude, and Canva to get the most from each tool?

Register today. Attend one or all the parts in the series. 

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.desc:
The Pickerington Public Library Board of Trustees meetings are held on the third Monday of the month, unless the 3rd Monday falls on a holiday, then the meeting is held on the 4th Monday.

The public is welcome to attend and sign in for public participation.

The Finance Advisory Board Committee meets 30 minutes prior to most regular Board meetings.

events.title: Monday Makers - DIY Bath Fizzies
events.desc:
What makes a bath bomb fizz? There’s a little science behind the bubbles!

Satisfy your curiosity at our December Monday Makers class. Create homemade bath fizzies using common household supplies and the special ingredient that makes them fizz. Then personalize your creations with essential oils, dried flowers, and other fun surprises.

All supplies are provided. Registration is required.

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.title: Winter Solstice Hike at Mambourg Park
events.address: 5531 Cincinnati Zanesville Road Northeast, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
What better way to spend the longest night of the year than on a lantern hike in the woods? Join Mambourg Park for a winter solstice hike on the Hickory Trail. Then, warm up with a hot cocoa by the fire inside the nature center. This program is for ages 13 and up. Meet inside the Nature Center.

events.desc: Bring your knitting, crochet, or other crafting project to work on while meeting with friends in this casual, self-guided gathering. Bring your own supplies and share your skills or learn from others. Not instructor led. No registration necessary.

events.desc:
Join Teen Writing Group to connect with other teen writers. Teen Writing Group is a friendly environment to share what you're working on, receive feedback, and grow as a writer. Each month, we'll explore a different writing style or genre, create stories based on a prompt, or collaborate on our writing struggles. 

Teen Writing Group meets on the 4th Tuesday of the month.

If you need accommodations for a class or event, contact communications@pickeringtonlibrary.org or call 614-837-4104 ext. 221.

events.desc:
Crafts with Crafts happens every Tuesday at 6 p.m. at Double Edge Brewing! Once a month they will do a guided craft class, then all other weeks are bring your own craft and hang! Forgot supplies? They’ll have a box of free crafts to keep you busy. No pressure to drink—though they’ve got plenty of beer, cider, cocktails & NA options, as well as a food truck on site to fill your hunger needs. Come craft, hang, and make some new friends!

For more information, please visit Double Edge Brewing’s Facebook page.

events.title: Combustion RUN at Combustion Brewery
events.address: 80 West Church Street, Pickerington, Ohio 43147, United States
events.desc:
Join Combustion Brewery & Taproom for Combustion RUN, kicking off every Tuesday from the taproom at 6:30 p.m! You’ll move together along a three mile paved loop through Pickerington before returning to Combustion where you can enjoy fresh bevvies from the brewery, a meal from the food truck, dinner from a local business, or all three! If you’re not up for three miles, do less, and if you’re itching to go long, do more; they’re not there to judge. Pace doesn’t matter – as long as you’re moving, they’re here for it!

 

For more information, please visit Combustion Brewery’s Facebook page.

events.title: November Project Scioto Mile Free Workout
events.desc:
November Project is a free outside fitness group that started in Boston in 2011 to break down barriers to movement! Now in 53 cities around the globe, we create free, fun, scalable (adjustable to your fitness level) workouts for all ages – and doggos!

Our workout starts at 6:14a every Wednesday morning in Genoa Park on the Scioto Mile (on the steps behind COSI). We work out for 45 minutes together until 7am, then walk down to One Line Coffee to hang out before work!

Come join us if you’re an off-the-couch fitness newbie, a runner looking to cross-train, or any fitness level in between, we’d love to see you!

events.title: Ask the Tech Trainer
events.desc:
Not sure what to do with that new device? Locked out of an account? Struggling to figure out your mobile phone? Meet with Guiding Ohio Online Technology Trainer Andrew for one-on-one assistance with a variety of technology topics. Drop in between 10 am and 4 pm or schedule an appointment online: https://appt.link/FPLTechHelp

This project was made possible in part by the Institute of Museum and Library Services and the State Library of Ohio.

events.desc:

Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned player, come to sharpen your skills, meet fellow chess enthusiasts, and have fun—no registration required! Chess sets provided.

events.title: Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief’s Tribute to America’s Warriors
events.desc:
The National Veterans Memorial and Museum (NVMM) will host Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief’s Tribute to America’s Warriors, a collection of original paintings by former President George W. Bush. The exhibition opens to the public on August 8, 2026.

The exhibition features more than 60 portraits of post-9/11 service members and Veterans, each one hand painted by President Bush and paired with a personal story of service, sacrifice, and resilience written by the former president.

The NVMM is open Thursday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
